title: Introduce windowed signal denoiser and adaptive failover policy for variable traffic
author: Maya Patel
description:
Motivation: Our continuous perf canary pipeline is sensitive to short, high-magnitude bursts and noisy client-side variance which produce false-positive regressions and unnecessary rollbacks. This PR introduces a windowed signal denoiser and a tiered adaptive failover policy to reduce noise-induced alerts while preserving sensitivity to sustained regressions.

What this PR does: Implements a Tukey-weighted sliding-window denoiser with robust median/IQR trimming, integrates a cross-cohort smoothing layer for low-traffic tenants, and adds a staged failover controller that performs: 1) soft-fallback to a cheaper model variant or cached responses, 2) traffic corking at cohort-level, and 3) last-resort rollback. The controller includes a 'staged-escape' detector that disables denoising if smoothed signals decorrelate from raw signal for N windows (prevents hiding true regressions).

Why this approach: Tukey tapering reduces influence of isolated outliers compared to simple EWMA; the robust central tendency preserves step changes while reducing spike sensitivity. Cross-cohort smoothing borrows statistical strength from similar traffic slices to avoid noisy signals for small tenants. Tiered failover provides graceful degradation and gives operators time to investigate before a hard rollback.

Testing performed: Unit tests for denoiser edge cases, integration tests plugging the denoiser into the canary evaluator, and e2e perf scenarios using the synthetic traffic harness (single-spike, burst trains, traffic ramp, and gradual model drift). Benchmarks run across three hardware profiles. Telemetry validated in staging and dashboards added for signal inspection.

Rollout plan: Feature-flag gated (canary_denoiser.enabled=false by default). Staged rollout: 1) enable for internal test tenants (1h), 2) enable for 5% of canaries (24h), 3) enable progressively to 50%+ after monitoring. If anomalies occur, toggle feature-flag off to revert instantly.

Checklist:
- [x] Algorithm implementation (denoiser) and unit tests
- [x] Integration into canary pipeline and evaluator
- [x] Telemetry and dashboards
- [x] Runbook and rollback steps
- [x] Performance microbench and e2e verification

Notes: This PR touches only evaluation logic and controller paths; there are no public API changes. See linked Linear tasks for background (ENG-5421 describes noise patterns; ENG-5503 requested staged failover).

review_comments:
Liam Chen: Can you explain why we prefer Tukey-style weights vs exponential smoothing for short bursts?
Response: The Tukey taper reduces sensitivity to single outliers and preserves step changes; we include an adaptive lambda that shifts toward exponential smoothing when sustained drift is observed.

Rosa Vega: Telemetry cardinality looks high; consider aggregating percentiles at cluster-level.
Response: Aggregation added and new metric canary_signal_bucket now emitted at 5m granularity to avoid cardinality explosion. See internal/telemetry/canary_metrics.go for implementation.

Anand Iyer: We need safety gates for release; what happens if denoiser hides signal prior to rollback?
Response: Added 'staged-escape' detection that disables denoiser if decorrelation between raw and smoothed >= threshold for 3 windows; controller will evaluate raw signal and escalate directly to rollback if necessary.

release_notes:
- Add windowed denoiser to canary pipeline to stabilize latency signals under bursty traffic
- Introduce adaptive failover policy with staged soft-fallback before full rollback
- New telemetry: denoiser_signal_strength, denoiser_disabled_reason, failover_state
- Runbook: docs/runbooks/perf-canary-denoiser.md
risk_and_rollback: This change affects canary evaluation logic only; default feature flag is off for 1 week of gradual rollout. If regressions appear, flip canary_denoiser.enabled=false and the pipeline will revert to previous signal path. Emergency rollback tested in staging with toggle and verified in 30s.
testing_summary: E2E: synthetic traffic scenarios including single-spike bursts, multi-burst patterns, and gradual drift. Results: false-positive rate reduced from 6.3% to 0.9% on test corpus; detection latency unchanged. Benchmarks: CPU overhead approx +2% per controller replica; memory +30MB. Load tests run at 2x production load for 24h.
changelog: Notable: new metrics and config flags; no user-facing API change; internal rollout guard added under feature flag.
notes_for_reviewers: Focus on the failure modes section in denoiser.go and controller.go; pay attention to the staged-escape logic and telemetry aggregation to control cardinality.
